pr.title: fix(factory): relax Bindings and Variables for `createMiddleware`

summary: This PR relaxes the type signature of createMiddleware so that Bindings/Variables not explicitly specified default to `any` instead of `{}`, avoiding spurious type errors when composing middleware with partial Env generics. It's a type-only change with no runtime logic modification, but it widens type safety by substituting `any` for missing Bindings/Variables, which could mask legitimate type errors in some codebases.

findings.rationale: Replacing default `{}` with `any` for unspecified Bindings/Variables loosens type checking broadly for all createMiddleware usages, which could suppress genuine type errors for users who rely on strict typing of c.env or c.var in middleware without generics.
findings.suggestedCheck: Verify existing test suite and downstream consumers don't rely on strict type errors being thrown for mismatched Bindings/Variables now that they resolve to `any`.

findings.rationale: The added test only checks that the code compiles/runs without throwing a TypeScript error; it doesn't verify that intentionally incompatible Bindings/Variables types still produce a type error, so the relaxation's boundary isn't tested.
findings.suggestedCheck: Add a compile-time negative test (e.g. using ts-expect-error) confirming that truly incompatible Env types still fail to type-check after this change.
